mergedParams.userDescription: Vintage film burn sprocket hole dust scratch transition effects between videos

output.title: Vintage Film Burn & Sprocket Hole Transitions

prompts.prompt: Create a vintage film burn transition preset that simulates authentic 16mm film damage during the transition period. The transition should feature a dramatic burn effect that appears to eat through the outgoing video frame while revealing the incoming video underneath. During the 1.5-second overlap period, apply a custom burn overlay video (film-burn-overlay.mp4) that plays at the transition point with a 'screen' blend mode. The outgoing video should develop increasing contrast and brightness irregularities (using filter animations) as if the film is literally burning, while the incoming video emerges through the burned areas with initial flickering and stabilization. Add authentic sprocket hole overlays on both sides of the frame using absolutely positioned ImageAtoms with vintage sprocket PNG assets. Include dust and scratch texture overlays that intensify during the transition using multiple ImageAtom layers with 'multiply' and 'overlay' blend modes. The transition should feel organic and unpredictable, with slight shake effects on both videos during the burn moment.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container with duration calculated as video1.duration + video2.duration - 1.5s overlap. Three main layers: outgoing VideoAtom (z-10), incoming VideoAtom (z-20), burn overlay VideoAtom (z-30, screen blend mode, plays only during overlap). Sprocket holes: Two ImageAtoms positioned absolutely (left-0 top-0 h-full w-16) and (right-0 top-0 h-full w-16) with sprocket PNGs. Dust/scratch overlays: 2-3 ImageAtom layers with multiply/overlay blend modes, opacity animated from 0 to 0.7 during transition. Effects: Outgoing video gets filter animation (brightness 100% to 150%, contrast 100% to 200%) and slight shake transform. Incoming video has opacity fade from 0 to 100% with initial shake that stabilizes. All effects use provider mode with targetIds for precise control.

prompts.prompt: Design a cinematic film splice transition that mimics the physical cutting and splicing of celluloid film strips. The transition should create the illusion that the outgoing video is being physically cut with visible splice marks, tape edges, and frame jumps characteristic of hand-spliced film. Implement a quick 0.3-second transition where the last few frames of the outgoing video appear to stutter and jump (using rapid opacity flickers and position shifts), followed by a hard cut to the incoming video that starts with 2-3 frames of black/clear film leader. Add authentic film artifacts including visible splice tape texture (as a semi-transparent ImageAtom overlay), frame registration marks that briefly appear during the splice, and subtle gate weave movement on both videos. Include period-appropriate dust particles that accumulate near the splice point, creating a sense of physical film handling.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with minimal 0.3s overlap for hard-cut feel. Outgoing VideoAtom plays until splice point with stutter effect: opacity keyframes [100%, 0%, 100%, 50%, 0%] over final 0.2s, plus transform translateX random shifts (-2px to 2px). Black leader: Shape/ImageAtom with black fill, appears for 0.1s during transition. Incoming VideoAtom starts immediately after leader. Splice tape overlay: ImageAtom with tape texture PNG, absolute positioning at transition point, opacity 0.6, appears only during splice moment. Gate weave: Both videos have subtle transform animations (translateX and translateY ±1-2px on sine wave pattern). Dust particles: 3-4 small ImageAtoms with dust PNGs, animated opacity and slight drift movement near splice point.

prompts.prompt: Build a dramatic projector malfunction transition that simulates vintage film projector failures with burning frames, melting emulsion, and mechanical stuttering. The 2-second overlap should begin with the outgoing video suddenly freezing on a single frame (using endAt to stop playback), then rapidly degrading as if the projector bulb is burning through the stuck film. Apply extreme color distortion effects progressing from normal to completely blown-out whites and deep burned oranges/browns. The incoming video should appear to struggle to start, with initial frames showing projector gate flicker, unstable brightness, and mechanical jitter before stabilizing. Add authentic projector elements including visible gate masks, flickering projector light spill around edges, and the characteristic sound of film slipping through the gate (if using AudioAtom).
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 2s overlap period. Outgoing VideoAtom: plays normally then freezes using endAt property at transition start. Apply filter animations: brightness (100% to 300%), contrast (100% to 250%), sepia (0% to 80%), blur (0px to 3px). Color overlay: ShapeAtom with orange/brown gradient, opacity animates 0% to 60% during burn. Incoming VideoAtom: starts with rapid opacity flicker [0%, 100%, 20%, 100%, 50%, 100%] over first 0.5s, plus transform scale oscillation (0.98 to 1.02) for projector shake. Gate mask: Black ShapeAtom frame with center cutout using absolute positioning and higher z-index. Light spill effect: Blurred white ShapeAtom behind videos, opacity pulses during transition.

prompts.prompt: Develop a film reel change transition that recreates the experience of switching between two film reels in a vintage cinema projection booth. The transition should show the tail leader of the outgoing reel with authentic countdown marks, registration crosses, and reel-end indicators, followed by the head leader of the incoming reel with its own set of technical marks and frame numbers. Include a brief moment of 'dead air' (black screen with only projector noise) between reels as would occur during manual reel changes. Add period-specific elements like cigarette burns (cue marks) in the upper right corner that signal the projectionist to start the second projector, visible perforations along the edges, and authentic SMPTE leader graphics.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with extended 3s transition for full reel change effect. Outgoing VideoAtom plays until reel end. Countdown leader: Series of ImageAtoms or TextAtoms showing numbers 3-2-1 with precise 1s intervals, positioned centrally. Cue marks: Small white circular ShapeAtoms (10px diameter) at top-right corner, appear twice (8s and 1s before reel end). Black gap: 0.5s period with black BaseLayout background between reels. Incoming leader: Similar countdown structure but ascending, with registration marks (cross-hair ImageAtoms). Perforation overlay: Repeating ImageAtom pattern along left/right edges using CSS repeat-y. All leaders use high z-index above video content. Timing uses fitDurationTo for precise reel change synchronization.

prompts.prompt: Create an authentic optical printer transition that simulates the layered, multiple-exposure effects used in vintage film post-production. The transition should create a double-exposure effect where both videos are visible simultaneously through different blend modes and opacity levels, mimicking the optical printing process where multiple film strips are combined. During the 1.8-second overlap, implement a complex layering system where the outgoing video gradually becomes more transparent while simultaneously applying color channel separation (RGB split effect using multiple copies with color filters). The incoming video should fade in with initial overexposure and color bleeding, gradually normalizing. Include film lab artifacts like edge fogging, chemical stains (organic shape overlays), and the distinctive look of optical printer alignment marks.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 1.8s overlap, containing multiple video layers. Outgoing video: Three VideoAtom copies for RGB split (each with filter hue-rotate at 0°, 120°, 240°), slight position offset (±2-4px), opacity fading from 100% to 0%. Incoming VideoAtom: Initial opacity 0% to 100%, with filter animations for brightness (150% to 100%) and saturation (150% to 100%). Edge fogging: Gradient ShapeAtoms at frame edges with white-to-transparent radial gradients, opacity 0.3-0.5. Chemical stains: 2-3 ImageAtoms with organic blob PNGs, blend mode 'overlay', subtle opacity animation. Alignment marks: Small cross ImageAtoms at corners, visible briefly during transition. All videos use absolute positioning with precise z-index layering.

prompts.prompt: Design a vintage film strip slide transition where the entire frame appears to physically slide horizontally like film advancing through a projector gate, complete with visible sprocket holes, frame lines, and the next frame partially visible at the edge. The transition should show the mechanical movement of film through the gate with authentic details like slight vertical instability (gate weave), momentary exposure of the frame line between shots, and the characteristic motion blur that occurs during rapid film advance. Implement realistic physics where the slide accelerates and decelerates following an ease-in-out curve, with a brief moment where both frames are partially visible in the gate.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 0.8s overlap for slide movement. Container uses 'overflow-hidden' to mask sliding motion. Outgoing VideoAtom: transform translateX animation from 0 to -100% with ease-in-out timing. Incoming VideoAtom: positioned at translateX(100%), animates to translateX(0) synchronized with outgoing. Frame line: Vertical black ShapeAtom (2-4px wide) positioned between videos, visible during slide. Sprocket holes: ImageAtom overlay that moves with the videos, showing continuous sprocket pattern. Gate weave: Both videos have subtle translateY animation (±1-2px) with sine wave pattern. Motion blur: During peak slide velocity (middle 0.3s), apply slight horizontal blur filter (1-2px). Brief double-exposure: At midpoint, both videos at 70% opacity for 0.1s to simulate gate exposure overlap.

prompts.prompt: Build a deteriorating film stock transition that progressively degrades from pristine to heavily damaged film, simulating years of wear, chemical deterioration, and poor storage conditions. The outgoing video should develop increasing amounts of vinegar syndrome artifacts (wavy distortions), color fading (particularly in reds/magentos), and emulsion bubbling effects. As the damage peaks, the incoming video emerges from beneath the deteriorating layer, initially showing its own wear patterns before gradually clearing up. Include authentic aging effects like silver mirroring (metallic sheen in dark areas), base scratches that accumulate over time, and the characteristic brittleness artifacts of deteriorating acetate film.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 2.5s overlap for gradual deterioration. Outgoing VideoAtom: Progressive filter animations - sepia (0% to 40%), contrast (100% to 70%), brightness (100% to 130%). Warping effect: CSS transform with slight skew and scale distortions animated over time. Emulsion bubbles: Multiple small circular ShapeAtoms with blur and reduced opacity, randomly positioned and animated. Silver mirroring: Gradient overlay ShapeAtom with metallic gradient in dark areas, opacity 0% to 30%. Scratches: Multiple thin ShapeAtoms (1px wide) with varying lengths, opacity increases over time. Incoming VideoAtom: Starts with moderate damage (sepia 20%, slight blur), cleans up over 1s. Vinegar syndrome waves: Transform-based distortion using multiple keyframes for wave-like motion.

prompts.prompt: Create a film jam/tear transition that simulates the dramatic moment when film gets caught in the projector mechanism and tears apart. The outgoing video should suddenly freeze, develop a bright white hotspot (from the projector bulb), then appear to tear diagonally across the frame with realistic torn edge geometry. The tear should reveal the incoming video underneath, which initially shows signs of mechanical stress (stretching, distortion) before snapping back to normal. Add authentic details like melting emulsion effects around the tear, visible film base showing through, and fragments of the torn film floating away from the tear line.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 1.2s dramatic overlap. Outgoing VideoAtom: Freezes using endAt, then opacity masks using CSS clip-path polygon to create torn edge shape. Hotspot: Radial gradient ShapeAtom (white center to transparent), positioned at tear origin, opacity 0% to 80%. Tear edge: SVG path or clip-path with jagged edge geometry, animates across frame diagonally. Melting effect: Blur and brightness filters intensify near tear edge (blur 0 to 5px, brightness 100% to 200%). Incoming VideoAtom: Initial transform scale(1.1, 0.9) for stretch effect, animates to scale(1, 1) with spring easing. Film fragments: 3-4 small ImageAtoms with torn film piece PNGs, animate with physics-based movement (gravity fall + slight rotation). Z-index carefully managed for proper layering.

prompts.prompt: Develop a multi-projector changeover transition that recreates the classic two-projector system used in theaters, complete with changeover cues, brief double-image overlap, and authentic projection booth elements. The transition should show the first projector's image gradually dimming while the second projector's image fades up, with a critical moment where both images are visible but slightly misaligned (simulating manual projector alignment). Include realistic projection artifacts like visible light cones, dust particles in the beam, subtle keystoning from projector angles, and the characteristic flicker of carbon arc lamps.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 1.5s changeover overlap. Outgoing VideoAtom: Opacity fade from 100% to 0% over 1.5s, slight transform scale(1.02) and rotate(0.5deg) for misalignment. Incoming VideoAtom: Opacity 0% to 100%, opposite misalignment with scale(0.98) and rotate(-0.5deg), corrects to normal at end. Light cone effects: Two translucent cone-shaped ShapeAtoms using CSS clip-path, slight opacity animation for flicker. Dust particles: Multiple small white circular ShapeAtoms animating through the 'light beam' area with varying speeds and opacity. Changeover cues: Motor cue (circle) and changeover cue (oval) ShapeAtoms in top-right, appear at specific times. Arc lamp flicker: Rapid brightness filter oscillation (98% to 102%) on both videos. Keystone correction: Subtle perspective transform on videos during overlap.

prompts.prompt: Design a chemical fade transition that mimics the look of film stock that has been chemically treated or partially developed, creating organic, unpredictable fade patterns between shots. The transition should feature irregular color shifts from chemical reactions, solarization effects where parts of the image invert, and organic blob-like shapes where chemicals have pooled or reacted differently across the film surface. The outgoing video should appear to be eaten away by chemical processes with realistic color degradation (cyans fading first, then magentas, leaving yellow-orange cast), while the incoming video emerges through the chemical fog with initial color instability before normalizing.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 2s overlap for organic chemical effect. Outgoing VideoAtom: Complex filter animations - individual color channel adjustments using CSS filters (red 100% to 60%, green 100% to 40%, blue 100% to 20%). Solarization: Invert filter animating in waves (0% to 50% to 0%) at random frame areas using mask-image gradients. Chemical blob masks: 3-4 ShapeAtoms with organic blob shapes (using SVG paths or border-radius distortions), blend mode 'difference' or 'exclusion', opacity and size animations. Incoming VideoAtom: Initial color cast (sepia 30%, saturate 150%), normalizes over 1s. Chemical pooling: Gradient overlays using radial-gradient ShapeAtoms, positioned randomly, opacity and blur animations. Edge effects: Feathered masks on video edges showing chemical burn patterns. Use CSS custom properties for coordinated color shift timings.
